heard: NASA caught speeding comet dust inside ultra-low-density silica aerogel. Launched in 1999, Stardust traveled 3 billion miles over seven years. To capture particles without destroying them on impact, engineers deployed a collector tray shaped like a tennis racket. In January 2004, the spacecraft swept past Comet Wild 2 to gently catch microscopic cosmic grains. On January 15, 2006, its sample return capsule descended under parachutes directly into the Utah desert. In Houston, the dust revealed various organic compounds. The Stardust at Home project let the public search for tracks. Volunteers identified seven rare interstellar dust particles trapped inside the aerogel. A volunteer found that interstellar grain, but how was it saved?
